# Social Studies course — CURRICULUM (the path)

Social Studies is one world course, organised by **levels, not
grades**: a learner climbs when they are ready, not when a
school calendar says so. The school grades the books come from
appear only in each lesson's sources (provenance), never as the
course's organisation. The path climbs from the learner's own
ground outward (see TITLES.md): **First Steps → Earth and Space
→ Population, Transport and Maps → People and Resources →
Ethiopia: Ancient and Medieval → Africa to 1500 → The Ancient
World → The Land and Air → Culture and Work → Resources and
Conflict → Modern Ethiopia → Africa after 1500 → The Modern
World → Global Issues**.

**The first page (what learners are told):** everything in this
course comes from government textbooks — this part from
Ethiopia's Social Studies books for Grades 7 and 8 — except the
**Tip boxes**: a tip in a box is from us, the people making
LiqLearns. Tips are ours; the lessons are the books'. See
ABOUT.md for the full book list, the pairing warning (Addis
Ababa guides against Amhara student books), the truncated
Grade 8 guide, and the acceptance reckoning.

measured; the literary track then treats geography as a
discipline (G10 foundations and techniques, G11

## Nicaragua — Geography expansion (merged 2026-11-15)
326 placement lines stocked from Nicaragua's 33 records
/ 13 distinct books. All 13 books are Spanish student
books of the Ministerio de Educación (MINED),
Nicaragua, all COMPLETE; Book 1 was read in place at
phase3-staging and Books 2–13 via the GitHub Releases
API route (grab.py), byte-size verified. The placements
file's header total and per-book tallies sum to exactly
326, matching the placement-line count — no tally
discrepancy. The file's split is 279 existing-flagged /
47 NEW-flagged (21 distinct NEW slugs); by lesson dir,
281 placements land in 83 standing lessons and 45 in
the 20 new lessons: one NEW-flagged slug already stands
as a lesson
(population-transport-and-maps/political-division-of-the-americas,
built by the Honduras merge) and its 2 placements are
stocked there, not rebuilt; no placement is remapped —
every existing-flagged slug stands. Book 10's record
name 'Primera Parte' is a misnomer carried exactly: the
book is the COMPLETE Grade 8 distance-learning module,
the parallel edition of Book 9. The non-Geography parts
of the combined books (History, Civics, Economics) are
named in the placements headers only, not placed.
Nicaragua's own way: Geography begins hyper-locally —
the child's own school, municipality and landscape, the
country introduced through its two great lakes
(Cocibolca and Xolotlán) as the 'land of lakes and
volcanoes' — then widens grade by grade: G3–G4 a full
national Geography at comunidad/municipio/departamento
scales, G5 the Central American isthmus, G6 the world
continents in one repeated template, G7 national
Geography closing on natural-risk prevention, G8 the
American continent, G9 the continents one by one, and
G10 the national Geography deepened, closing on
vulnerability and SINAPRED; distance-learning
self-study modules parallel the classroom books at G7,
G8, G9 (Geography only) and G10, every topic anchored
in the learner's own comunidad. Stocked into standing
lessons (281 placements across 83 lessons). 20 NEW
lessons built (45 placements) — **First Steps**: My

## Bhutan — Geography expansion (merged 2026-11-15)
349 placement lines stocked from Bhutan's 14 records /
9 distinct books. All 9 books are English student books
of the Royal Government of Bhutan (Center for School
Curriculum Development / Department of School
Education, Ministry of Education and Skills
Development), all COMPLETE; G4–G5 were read via the
grab.py tree route and G6–G12 via the records' ministry
(rec.gov.bt) source URLs after the grab.py route hung
on G6 — every book verified by pdfinfo with byte size +
page count matching its books.json record exactly, plus
cover/title-page render. The placements file's header
total and per-book tallies sum to exactly 349, matching
the placement-line count — no tally discrepancy. The

lessons: two NEW-flagged slugs already stand as lessons
(earth-and-space/the-rock-cycle and
population-transport-and-maps/models-of-urban-structure,
1 placement each) and their placements are stocked

existing-flagged slug stands. The non-Geography parts
of the combined Social Studies books IV–VI
(Religion/History, Civics, Health/Life Skills) are
named in the placements headers only, not placed.
Bhutan's own way: Social Studies IV–VI integrates
Geography with Civics, Culture, Economics, History and
Religion, taught from the child's home, village and
district outward with Bhutanese materials and local
forest and hazard examples; Grade 5 anchors world
geography in Bhutan's own map (location, three physical
zones, neighbours, major rivers, protected areas) and
Grade 6 adds Bhutan's climate zones, hydropower,
urbanisation and glacial lake outburst floods (GLOF);
from Class VII Geography is a standalone subject in
three strands (Time and Space; Physical Environment;
People and Environment), every world topic closed with
its Bhutan case; the Intermediate level (IX–X) treats
each world topic at full textbook depth with the Bhutan
case inside it, and the Advanced level (XI–XII) is full
academic geography — map projections, remote sensing
and GIS, climate classification — with Bhutan applied
chapters on agriculture, manufacturing and tourism, the
last taught on Bhutan's own sustainability principle
("high value, low volume"). Stocked into standing
lessons (207 placements across 126 lessons). 119 NEW

## Greece — Geography expansion (merged 2026-11-15)
599 placement lines stocked from Greece's 34 records /
17 distinct books (all Greek, Ministry of Education /
ITYE Diophantos). The placements file's per-book
tallies sum to exactly 599, matching the placement-line
count book by book, and its existing/NEW split
(134/465) agrees with the line flags (134
existing-flagged / 465 NEW-flagged, 179 distinct NEW
slugs) — no discrepancy. By lesson dir, 138 placements
land in 41 standing lessons and 461 in the 177 new
lessons. Two NEW-flagged slugs already stand as lessons
(global-issues/the-shrinking-aral-sea, 2 placements;
the-land-and-air/antarctica-the-frozen-continent, 2
placements — 4 placements in all) and their placements
are stocked there, not rebuilt. Two placements are
remapped from 2 existing-flagged slugs that do not
stand to the closest standing lesson covering the thing
(original slug recorded in each provenance row):
people-and-resources/economic-activities-the-three-levels
->
culture-and-work/economic-activities-the-three-levels
(1); the-land-and-air/materials-of-the-crust ->
earth-and-space/materials-of-the-crust (1). Books 1, 4,
10 and 14 are teacher guides (194 placements), cited as
teacher-guide evidence only, outside acceptance counts;
the workbooks (Books 3, 5, 9 and 12) carry STUDENT on
their Grade lines and count as student books. Every
standing destination takes at least one student-book
placement, so Greece counts in all 41 standing lessons;
5 new lessons stand on a teacher guide only (acceptance
count 0 countries). Books 6 and 16 are parallel revised
editions with 0 placements counted — their placements
are filed once under Books 2 and 11, both editions
named in those book entries. Books 7 and 8 (Social &
Political Education, Grades 5 and 6) are RECORD ONLY —
pure Civics, no Geography parts to place; a later
Civics wave owns them. Greece's own way: the primary
course studies one country whole — Grade 5 is 'Learning
Greece' (maps first, then Greece's natural environment,
then its human environment, closing outward to the EU,
Cyprus and the Greek diaspora) and Grade 6 turns
outward to the whole Earth ('Learning about the Earth':
Earth in space, the natural environment, how humans
live in deserts, polar lands, rainforests and temperate
zones, then a continent-by-continent tour, Europe first
and in depth); the Gymnasium course (Grades 7–8) is
organised by Earth's spheres in Grade 7 and gives the
whole of Grade 8 to one continent — Europe — with
Greece re-entered inside every theme; the EPAL Grade 12
book reads the world as tourism destinations, Greece
first and region by region. Stocked into standing
lessons (138 placements across 41 lessons). 177 NEW
lessons built (461 placements) — **The Land and Air**:

European whaling in the Pacific
(modern-world/european-whaling-in-the-pacific)
— 10 placements stocked from Tuvalu's three regional

Pacific — Book 1*, Years 5–6 student reader (Institute
of Education, University of the South Pacific (Tonga
Campus) with UNESCO, sponsored by the Japanese
Funds-in-Trust, 2020, no ISBN printed): "The Ocean in

Samoa, Tonga, Niue, Rotuma, Tokelau, Tuvalu, Futuna
and Uvea once one large exchange community, peoples
voyaging between islands circulating wealth, skills
and goods (printed pp. 1–2), stocked into the existing
Ancient World lesson Pacific voyaging and island
exchange — a NEW LESSON NEEDED placement in the
Tuvalu file, stocked into the lesson built for the
same topic in the Nauru merge instead of building a
duplicate; sharks, turtles and whales in Pacific
culture, with the sacred Tongan shark-noosing ritual
and turtle taboos (printed pp. 6–10), and traditional
uses of the reef and ocean with Tuvalu's own
practices on Nukufetau (printed pp. 12–15), into the
existing First Steps heritage lesson; and whales
after the Europeans came — Pacific people used only
stranded whales, teeth for chiefs' necklaces, until
North American whaling fleets reached Tonga in the
1890s and hunted mothers and calves, driving the
whales near extinction in one century before legal
protection let them slowly recover (printed p. 10),
into the new lesson. *People and the Natural
Environment in the Pacific — Book 3*, Years 5–6
student reader (same publisher, 2020): knowledge
passed down through generations (printed p. 6),
Tuvalu's pulaka pits (printed pp. 7–9) and the
amazing coconut tree, with Tuvalu's red toddy
(printed pp. 11–13), all into the heritage lesson.
*Teacher Guide for the ESD Readers — Years 5–8*,
teacher guide (same publisher, 2020), cited as
evidence only: pupils sent to talk to an elder, list
traditional fishing practices and find a legend of
the turtle, whale or shark (printed pp. 16–20), into
the existing First Steps
find-history-in-your-own-locality lesson — Tuvalu is
not added to that lesson's count, as the guide is
evidence only; the Book 3 inheritance notes (printed
pp. 24–28) and the Tuvalu-specific notes — the closed
Namo lagoon, storytelling and fatele song, and
Culture and Heritage in the Tuvalu National
Curriculum Framework (printed pp. 38–41) — into the
heritage lesson as evidence. Tuvalu was not counted
in the heritage lesson before, so its acceptance
count rises 18 → 19 countries, and in the Pacific
voyaging lesson 2 → 3 countries. Library debt, as
filed: Tuvalu's shelf holds no Tuvalu national
history book at all — only these regional readers,
the same set also shelved under Nauru and Niue.
History lessons: 270 → 271.

HONESTY: all nine books are student books, so every placement counts in acceptance; there are no teacher guides in this set. Combined books: Book 1 (SD-G4, History and National Education) — its Civics unit (Unit 4, We are Sudanese, printed pp. 53–70) and the Geography location half of Unit 3, Lesson 1 are named in its book entry, not placed; Book 3 (Grade 5) — Unit 5, The Art of National Education (Civics, printed pp. 106–120) is named, not placed; Book 4 (Grade 7) — Unit 2, Lesson 1 (Geography of the Arabian Peninsula) and Unit 3, Lesson 1 (Africa: The Natural Environment) are named, not placed; Book 8 (Grade 6) — Unit 5, National Education (Civics, printed pp. 69–80) is named, not placed. Books 1–2 (SD-G4, SD-G9) were downloaded from external Google Drive link records and staged in phase3-staging under the push-don't-delete rule, as filed in their book entries. Book 2 (SD-G9) was read from 100-DPI page renders because its text layer is broken-encoded; Books 8–9 (Grades 6 and 8) were read from page renders because their PDFs are image-only scans — all as filed. Count reconciliation: the placements file's per-book tallies sum to 208, but the file holds 207 placement lines and all 207 are stocked. Book 7 (Grade 12) is the source of the difference — its tally claims 30 placements (7 to existing lessons, 23 NEW) while the book's section holds 29 lines (6 to existing lessons, 23 NEW): the NEW counts agree exactly, and one existing-lesson placement was counted in the tally but never written as a line of its own. Book 5 (Grade 10)'s tally split (8 to existing, 13 NEW) differs from its lines (9 without the NEW marker, 12 with it) because the tally counts africa-to-1500/egyptian-civilisation — a slug absent from the wave's slug list — as NEW although its line carries no NEW marker; the book's total (21) agrees. Four Book 9 (Grade 8) lines name slugs without the NEW marker that did not exist in the tree (the Baqt treaty, the Funj sultanate of Sennar, the Abdallab sheikhdom, Darfur — the Fur and Keira sultanates); those lessons are built new here under the named slugs. Stories and readings are stocked as plot summaries only, never transcribed. The Grade 10 book (Book 11 — g10 Historia de Venezuela Contemporánea) was read in place from phase3-staging by the reading wave and was not deleted (push-don't-delete already handled). One existing lesson, Find history in your own locality, already counted Venezuela from an earlier wave, so its 3 History placements are stocked as depth without raising its count (28, unchanged). Stories, myths and legends (including the Piaroa myth in Book 1) are stocked as plot summaries only, never transcribed. Venezuela's own way is content: history starts from the child's own day, family and street; contemporary history is taught through three axes — coffee, oil and violence — under a dependence thesis, with time taught as recurrent, not a straight line. HONESTY: the two split placement files were read and merged as one country — 16 books in greece-placements.md and 14 in greece-b-placements.md, 28 of them placed (the Grade 5 and Grade 6 Social & Political Education books are RECORD ONLY — pure Civics, no History placements). The per-book tallies sum to 952 (508 + 444) but the line-by-line count is 951: file B's G9 Modern & Contemporary History book tallies 70 while only 69 placement lines are written — 951 is the true stocked count, and every written line is stocked. All books are Greek student books from ΙΤΥΕ «Διόφαντος» / the Institute of Educational Policy, Ministry of Education, except three TEACHER thematic folders (15 placements: the Acropolis of Athens folder, Wealth & Poverty in Byzantine Society, and the Heraklion dossier) — every teacher-folder placement is cited as the evidence it is, labelled (teacher folder — evidence) in its provenance row, and counted nowhere in acceptance; four new lessons stand on teacher-folder evidence only (The Acropolis Of Athens Through Time, Philanthropy In Byzantium Church And Poor Relief, Venetian Heraklion A Fortress City, Heraklion Many Faiths One City) and carry no acceptance count. Greece was already counted in Heritage — what it is and why it matters from an earlier wave, so its 5 new placements are stocked there as depth without raising the count. Greece's own way is content: history begins as story — the Grade 3 book retells Greek myth as narrative (creation, heroes, Troy, Odysseus) before prehistory begins; the myths are stocked as the books tell them, as myth/story — plot summaries in the course's own words only, never transcribed.

File B's books are scanned-image PDFs with no text layer, read visually from rendered pages (cover, imprint, preface, full contents, unit/section openers, sampled spreads) — that sample-based reading stands exactly as filed in each book entry and is not upgraded to a full read. Four books are TEACHER guides (file A Books 10, 11 and 13; file B Book 15, with its Russian twin Book 16 placed under it) — their 139 placements are cited as the evidence they are, labelled (teacher guide — evidence) in every provenance row, and counted nowhere in acceptance; every lesson they touch also carries student-book placements, so no lesson stands on teacher evidence alone. Two file-B books are PARTIAL as filed (Book 5: the scan ends at printed p. 141, its closing glossary absent from the file; Book 9: the scan runs ~4 pages short of the printed pagination, a few pages skipped in scanning) and are labelled as filed. Glossary/terminology word lists are inventory-only: no glossary material is placed as a placement anywhere in this merge; glossaries are named in the book entries only. Kazakhstan's own way is content: NIS inquiry textbooks framing every section as a question with source work, and narrative surveys in the upper bands.

## Economics expansion — Belarus — built 2026-11-15

Belarus — 5 placements stocked from *Person. Society. State,
Grade 9 — Book 2 «Свет людзей» (The World of People)* (student
book, Belarusian, COMPLETE for the volume in hand; Народная
асвета (Narodnaya Asveta), Minsk, 2001; ISBN 985-12-0294-0;
name glossary pp. 230–238 inventory-only, named in the book
entries, not stocked). 2 stocked into standing lessons —
**Microeconomics**: Cost curves and profit (§28 At work —
profit (прыбытак) as enterprise income minus production
costs, net profit as what remains after taxes and payments
to the budget, and profit rising through rational use of
the factors of production, printed p. 216; now taught in 2
countries, Ethiopia and Belarus) and Opportunity cost (§29
The person as a consumer — the "price of choice" (цана
выбару): with limited life possibilities and money,
satisfying a need means giving something up, and the
rational consumer picks the variant whose price of choice
is lowest, printed p. 224; now taught in 2 countries,
Ethiopia and Belarus) — and 3 new lessons built (12
questions each) — in **Market and Money**: Wages — nominal
and real, piece-rate and time-rate (1 placement, §29,
printed p. 221 — wages as the price of labour: nominal wage
the money sum versus real wage the goods and services it
buys at a given price level, and the two main forms,
piece-rate (здзельная, per unit produced) and time-rate
(пачасовая, per hour actually worked), with bonuses and
profit-sharing on top); in **Macroeconomics**: The
subsistence minimum and the consumer basket (1 placement,
§29, printed p. 223 — consumption as using goods and
services to meet needs, its level set by personal income;
the subsistence minimum (пражытачны мінімум) and the
"consumer basket" (спажывецкі кошык) of typical goods and
services as the yardstick of living standards across
countries, from which the state sets the minimum wage);
and in **Microeconomics**: Consumer rights and protection
(1 placement, §29, printed p. 225 — the consumer's legal,
economic and social rights under Belarus's law on consumer
protection: quality goods, full information, free repair
or replacement of faulty goods, compensation — defended
by state bodies, courts and consumer societies). Belarus's
own way: economics arrives inside a philosophy-and-civics
course as the ethics of work — profit defined on one
diagram, then wages, the subsistence minimum and the
consumer basket as measures of a decent life. Economics
lessons: 380 → 383.

## Economics expansion — France — built 2026-11-16

France — 21 placements stocked from 1 student book
(SES 2de, Manuel Libre de Sciences économiques et
sociales, Seconde — an open-licensed HTML manual,
Les Manuels Libres; 2 records / 1 distinct book).
The filing's tally (19 to existing lessons + 2 NEW
LESSON NEEDED) matches the placement lines exactly
— no difference. The book is a student book in
French, so every placement counts in acceptance;
placements cite the chapter and section instead of
a printed page, the manual having no PDF pages.
19 stocked into standing lessons —
**Microeconomics**: What economics is (Ch. Method,
"Quelles questions se posent les économistes";
acceptance 1 → 2 countries); Opportunity cost
(Ch. Method, same section — "Qu'est-ce que le coût
d'opportunité"; acceptance 2 → 3); Production —
turning inputs into outputs (Ch. Richesses, "Que
produit-on ?" — market vs non-market production
through bakery, hairdressing, teaching and care
cases; acceptance 2 → 3); Land, labour, capital,
entrepreneurship (Ch. Richesses, "Comment
produit-on ?" — complementary and substitutable
factors and the most profitable combination;
acceptance 2 → 3); The law of demand (Ch. Marché —
tobacco prices and milk producers; acceptance
1 → 2); The law of supply (Ch. Marché — the
quinoa-in-Côte-d'Or case; acceptance 1 → 2);
Equilibrium price and quantity (Ch. Marché — the
lunch-deal market, oil prices and French housing;
acceptance 1 → 2); Pigouvian taxes, subsidies and
the Coase theorem (Ch. Marché — tax on buyer and
on producer, housing aid captured by landlords,
ecological taxation; acceptance 1 → 2) —
**Macroeconomics**: Expansionary fiscal policy
(Ch. Method — the France Relance plan read as a
Keynesian model; acceptance 1 → 2); Measuring GDP
— value added at every stage (Ch. Richesses,
"Principaux indicateurs" — a bicycle firm and
Nike's figures; acceptance 1 → 2); GDP — what a
country produces inside its borders (Ch. Richesses
— how INSEE computes growth; acceptance 1 → 2);
Measuring economic growth (Ch. Richesses — the
Malthusian trap, the Trente Glorieuses, world
growth since 1900; acceptance 1 → 2); Per-capita
GDP (Ch. Richesses, "Quelles sont les limites du
PIB ?" — GDP per inhabitant across Europe;
acceptance 1 → 2); What GDP misses (Ch. Richesses,
same section — inequality and the Angola oil case;
acceptance 1 → 2); Frictional, structural and
cyclical unemployment (Ch. Diplôme — unemployment
as a qualifications mismatch, rates by diploma;
acceptance 1 → 2) — **Market and Money**: Markets
and the market for goods and services (Ch. Marché,
"Qu'est-ce qu'un marché ?" — fruit-seller,
estate-agent, auction and art-market cases;
acceptance 1 → 2 countries, Ethiopia and France;
Guatemala remains teacher-guide evidence only);
Wage determination in the labour market
(Ch. Diplôme — salary by level of training/diploma;
acceptance 1 → 2 countries, Ethiopia and France;
Iceland remains teacher-guide evidence only) —
**Global Issues**: The economy and the environment
— sources and sinks (Ch. Richesses — the ecological
limits of growth, ecological footprint, species
loss and temperature/CO2 graphs; acceptance
5 → 6 countries) — **People and Resources**:
Functional and personal income distribution
(Ch. Diplôme, "Quelles inégalités face au
diplôme ?" — the gender pay gap in data, cadre
salaries, efficiency wages; acceptance 1 → 2).
2 new lessons built (12 questions each):
**Microeconomics**: Who produces — firms,
administrations and the social economy
(Ch. Richesses, "Qui produit ?" — enterprises
with a common structure, hierarchy and the
contract, public administrations, and the social
and solidarity economy, ESS) —
**Macroeconomics**: Investing in human capital
(Ch. Diplôme, "Les études, un investissement
rentable ?" — the cost of studies in France,
Europe and the USA against the returns in salary,
well-being and capabilities, and the role of
public education policy). France's own way: SES
teaches economics, sociology and political
science as one subject from Seconde; the economics
is built from data and cases (INSEE, the France
Relance plan read as a Keynesian model, housing
and oil prices, the gender pay gap in
spreadsheets) with a synthesis and exercise for
nearly every notion. Economics lessons:
404 → 406.

Economics lessons: 764 → 799.

Checked first: none of the 56 NEW slugs existed in the current tree, and no existing lesson covers these things — PNG's Trade-strand sequence (needs and wants by environment, cash crops, producers and consumers in the local community, formal versus informal activities, communication in trade from conch shell and kundu drum to mobile phone), its own tax system and national goals, its labour units, its ideology sequence (capitalism, communism and socialism each judged in turn) and its Grade 12 analytical topics (resource use through time, sales-tax incidence, the ILO, bilateral and multilateral relations, foreign aid, internet pricing) have no standing equivalents. Papua New Guinea's own way: Economics enters at Grade 3 as a Trade strand built from village life — a canoe is a need on the coast, not in the highlands; production is taught through making a food garden; trade starts with traditional exchange, shell money and pigs before modern money and EFTPOS; the senior courses re-run the frame at full depth with PNG's own institutions throughout — the IRC and a tax system funding about 75% of the budget, the Bank of Papua New Guinea's direct and indirect instruments, a public-service wage bill of over K200 million a fortnight, the Hiri-Motu trade, SMEC loans through the National Development Bank, the ICCC as consumer watchdog, and development judged against the Five National Goals and Directive Principles. Economics lessons: 998 → 1054.

Bhutan's own way: Economics is framed throughout by Gross National Happiness (GNH) — material vs spiritual well-being — and every concept is anchored in Bhutanese examples (ngultrum-era money history, hydropower exports to India, Kheng bamboo products, the Royal Monetary Authority, the Consumer Protection Act of Bhutan 2012, Bhutan's own named banks); Class X turns to Bhutan itself (the Bhutanese economy's features, public finance, GNH alongside GDP, the rupee-crisis case), Class XI adds Bhutan-specific system, Five-Year Plan and trade-policy chapters, and Class XII closes with Bhutan-flavoured public finance and national income as compiled by Bhutan's National Statistics Bureau. And 24 new lessons built (standard shape, 12 questions each): Microeconomics (5): Exceptions to the law of demand, Exceptions to the law of supply, Factor incomes — rent, interest and profit, Factor rewards — rent, interest and profit, Revenue — total, average and marginal; Market and Money (4): Bhutan's monetary history, Credit creation by commercial banks, Dignity of labour, E-commerce and digital trade; Macroeconomics (15): Balance-of-payments deficit — causes, effects and correction, Bhutan's economic system — features, Bhutan's economy — features and diversification, Bhutan's five-year plans, Bhutan's trade policy and agreements, Bhutan's trading partners and trade pattern, Challenges of the Bhutanese economy, Deficit financing, Economic growth versus development, Globalisation and liberalisation, Gross National Happiness as a development measure, Public debt and debt redemption, Public expenditure, Raising saving and investment in Bhutan, Statistics for economics — data and index numbers.
